conventions.convention: N ≥ 1; H_N = −h Σ Z_j − J Σ X_j X_{j+1}, with bonds only for j < N. The Majoranas are γ_{2j−1} = (Z_1⋯Z_{j−1})X_j and γ_{2j} = (Z_1⋯Z_{j−1})Y_j. The empty string is the identity.
Inner products are linear in the first argument. The finite chain uses the product inner product on (ℂ²)⊗N.
The skew normal form uses blocks [[0, ε_r], [−ε_r, 0]] with ε_r ≥ 0. Each positive block contributes two equal singular values; zero blocks pair kernel directions.
Countable Choice is assumed. The Fourier transform uses Σ_j x_j e^{ijk}, angle torus ℝ/(2πℤ), normalized Borel measure dk/(2π), and L² equivalence classes modulo almost-everywhere equality.
The finite trace theorem assumes Countable Choice, real h and J in joules, and β > 0 in inverse joules. Its skew-matrix entries are 2h and 2J, and each zero mode contributes a trace factor two.

The bulk gap is the minimum nonnegative band energy of the explicitly defined one-particle operator iA_∞. Its closing does not assert an infinite spin-chain ground-state uniqueness result or a thermodynamic-limit singularity.

load_bearing.statement: For integer N ≥ 1, define H_N(h,J) = −h Σ_{j=1}^N Z_j − J Σ_{j=1}^{N−1} X_jX_{j+1} on (ℂ²)⊗N, with ordered Majoranas γ_{2j−1} = S_{j−1}X_j and γ_{2j} = S_{j−1}Y_j.
Assume Countable Choice. For N ≥ 1, real h,J in joules and β > 0 in inverse joules, H_N = (i/4)γᵀA_Nγ = Σ_r ε_r(b_r* b_r − I/2), and Tr(e^{−βH_N}) = ∏_r 2 cosh(βε_r/2), including zero block energies.

Assume Countable Choice. The map F₀x(k) = Σ_j x_j e^{ijk} on finitely supported two-component lattice sequences preserves inner products and has a unique extension to a surjective linear isometry from ℓ²(ℤ;ℂ²) onto L²(𝕋;ℂ²).
For every integer N ≥ 1 and real h,J, each ordered Ising Majorana γ_a is Hermitian and γ_aγ_b + γ_bγ_a = 2δ_ab I for 1 ≤ a,b ≤ 2N.

For every integer N ≥ 1 and real skew-symmetric A ∈ M_{2N}(ℝ), there are a real orthogonal O and ε_1,…,ε_N ≥ 0 such that OAOᵀ is the direct sum of blocks [[0, ε_r], [−ε_r, 0]], with the stated singular-value multiplicities.

published_dependencies.used_for: Explicit Pauli matrices, linear-first inner product, adjoint and tensor-product conventions used in the chain definition and CAR calculation.
Finite Hermitian spectral decomposition, simultaneous diagonalization by invariant eigenspaces, spectral exponentials and basis-independent trace.
Finite fermionic occupation trace ∏_r(1 + e^{−βε_r}) at chemical potential zero; finite mode sets permit zero energies.
Exact Countable Choice assumption carried by the occupation-trace, Fourier and Hilbert-adjoint suppliers.
Scalar ℓ² pairing, finite-subset sums, reindexing and small-tail control used coordinatewise for lattice sequences.
Compact quotient torus, normalized Borel measure and integral, transported to the angle convention; positive measure of nonempty arcs.
Completeness and the linear-first integral pairing on complex L² under Countable Choice.
One-dimensional character basis, Parseval and surjective Fourier coefficient isometry; inverse Fourier series in the finite-subset-net sense.
Boundedness criterion for lattice shifts, the bulk operator and matrix multiplication operators.
Adjoint pairing convention and uniqueness used to identify shift adjoints and prove self-adjointness of iA_∞.
Spectrum as the complement of shifts λI − T possessing bounded everywhere-defined inverses.
